summary: The candidate accurately captures most of the paper's central mathematical chain from framed-link surgery and ribbon categories through ribbon Hopf algebras, modular data, purification, and the RT invariant. Formulas, page locators, and external attributions are generally strong. However, numerous lemma- or definition-level results are typed merely as calculations, several foundational Gold entries are absent as distinct entries, and the Kirby-invariance proof infrastructure is compressed into the final RT theorem. The negligible-module entry also makes an unjustified equivalence between vanishing quantum trace for every endomorphism and vanishing quantum dimension.
strengths: Faithfully extracts the Lickorish–Wallace theorem, Kirby calculus, Turaev ribbon-graph theorem, purification theorem, and final Reshetikhin–Turaev invariance theorem.
Preserves the principal formulas for the universal R-matrix, ribbon element, quantum trace, modular data, Kirby color, surgery sum, and signature normalization.
Accurately covers the categorical progression from monoidal structure and duality to braiding, ribbon structure, and the ribbon structure on finite-dimensional representations.
Page locators are valid and closely aligned with the source, while major literature-derived theorems are explicitly marked as external.
Includes several legitimate source entries beyond the Gold set, such as blackboard framing, categorical trace, the pivotal isomorphism, Yang–Baxter identity, and the colored Jones specialization.
issues: The standalone Hopf algebra definition in the Gold reference is missing.
The standalone definitions of twist, finite simple system/domination, Hopf-link S-matrix, negligible morphism, and purification are missing or only implicit inside broader entries.

The handle-slide invariance lemma, blow-up invariance lemma, Kirby-presentation-independence proposition, and the explicit reduction from Kirby invariance to a 3-manifold invariant are not extracted as distinct results.

Several mathematical results corresponding to Gold lemmas or definitions are classified as "calculation", including coproduct-induced monoidality, antipode-induced duality, R-matrix braiding, quantum trace, modular data, graphical calculus, and RT normalization.

The negligible-module statement incorrectly says that vanishing quantum trace for every endomorphism is equivalent to vanishing quantum trace of the identity; this equivalence does not hold for a general module without additional assumptions.
The colored framed-link invariant is classified as a definition even though the Gold reference treats its isotopy invariance as a proposition-level claim.
The final RT theorem absorbs several logically distinct invariance results, reducing the auditability and completeness of the extracted proof structure.

entryLevelComparison.note: Accurate statement and appropriate theorem classification.

No standalone definition of a Hopf algebra and its antipode identities.

The formula is accurate, but the lemma-level assertion is classified as a calculation.

The quotient construction appears inside the theorem, but purification is not delimited as its own definition.
Handle-slide invariance of the Kirby-color sum is not extracted separately.
The normalization's invariance under plus-or-minus-one blow-up moves is only implicit in the final theorem.
The normalization formula is correct, but it is classified as a calculation rather than a definition.
Correctly captures the main RT invariant and its dependence only on the oriented homeomorphism class.
